messages:
Casey: tiny WFH drama  tried to hide my router behind studio monitors for cleaner cable vibes. Calls started dropping mid-sentence. Photo: https://images.redwood.example/casey-monitor-router.jpg :headphones: :grimacing:

Ben: oof aesthetic vs reliability. Any quick diagnostics you can run while it hiccups?

Casey: Yeah ran a short ping during a freeze, pasted below. Spikes every few packets:

Casey: ```
$ ping -c 8 1.1.1.1
PING 1.1.1.1 (1.1.1.1): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=57 time=11.0 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=57 time=237.4 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=3 ttl=57 time=10.8 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=4 ttl=57 time=12.1 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=5 ttl=57 time=489.2 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=6 ttl=57 time=10.7 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=7 ttl=57 time=11.2 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=8 ttl=57 time=10.9 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
8 packets transmitted, 8 packets received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 10.7/100.5/489.2 ms
```

Priya: Those big intermittent spikes look like either RF attenuation from the monitor enclosure or EMI from the amp. Studio gear with big transformers can play havoc. First quick check: move the router 30cm away from speakers and test 5GHz if supported.

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed casey-laptop intermittent spikes between 2469999102-2469999188; peak RTT 490ms, 3 retransmits. Suggest: raise AP, try 5GHz, or temporary tether for meetings.

Luca: If you want to keep the look, try mounting the router on the top of the monitors with velcro so it's elevated and not behind the magnets. Also try flipping router orientation  antenna pattern is weird around speaker cabinets.

Sam: Another cheap trick: USB Wi-Fi dongle on a 0.5-1m extension cable and stick it on the bookshelf above the monitors. Raised antenna = fewer obstructions.

Casey: Poll: react with :musical_note: for "velcro-top-monitor", :arrow_up: for "raise on shelf", :phone: for "tether during calls". GIFs welcome.

Ben: Also check monitor power cable routing  running it parallel to the router ethernet or USB can introduce noise. Try re-routing if you see the spikes sync with amp activity.

Priya: If spikes persist after repositioning, check router firmware and logs for WAN flaps. If it's truly EMI from amp transformers, a ferrite clamp on the monitor power cable might help.

Casey: Quick update  used a short USB extension + dongle, perched it on the bookshelf. No more dropouts in a 50m call. Victory pic: https://images.redwood.example/casey-dongle-victory.jpg :tada:

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: casey-laptop events cleared at 2469999319; no retransmits in last 20m. Marking resolved.

Casey: Thanks team! Studio aesthetic preserved, calls stable, and the magnets didn't eat my wifi. Will accept punny router names in the thread. :guitar:
